messages.subject: Predicate fixed and tested; damage quantified with a new side-issue flagged
messages.body: Fixed _is_contents_entry in src/michael/ingest.py by making it context-aware: a trailing bare number is only a contents-table page reference when a real neighbouring line (threaded in via a new _adjacent_lines helper) also ends in one, since a cited Act year and a page number are the same shape and no string-only or year-range rule can tell them apart; all 9 required fixture cases pass in a new test, the existing suite is 150/150 green (149 before plus the new test), mypy is clean, and running split_sections on the real Privacy Act confirms 26WD is recovered with zero regressions. Step 2 (read-only, no DB write) found local Postgres unreachable this session so I measured against the same public wa+commonwealth corpus seed_from_corpus draws from instead of the exact 204-document set: a 27,700-document partial scan found 14,128 newly-kept headings and zero newly-lost ones, and a complete 3,000-document scan found 1,923 newly-kept headings (963 Act/Regulation, 960 case) across 1,107 affected documents with zero regressions, but also surfaced a new out-of-scope finding -- numbered footnote/citation lists in case-law judgments and a definitions cross-reference table in at least one Act get the same 'not a contents entry' treatment, which inflates the gain count with non-Part-IIIC-class rows I did not touch. Full diff, rule rationale, sourcing notes for every fixture string, and the complete per-document/per-heading breakdown are in the attached report; re-ingestion of the 204 documents and any fix for the footnote-list side effect are left for your and the owner's decision.
